mainText: This is Dose of Good for Wednesday, November 11. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Newborn stingray takes its first swim and returns to the sea in Greece. The pup was cared for until it was strong enough, then released into the Thermaic Gulf with a second chance at survival. Second: São Paulo outskirts schools turn rubble-filled lots into gardens and food forests. A University of São Paulo study followed schools that cleared vacant lots and planted vegetable gardens and agroforests, with before-and-after photos. Third: AI helps spot dangerous rip currents on Australian beaches. RipEye, a tool built by UNSW, is being trialled on New South Wales beaches to detect rip currents and keep swimmers safe. Fourth: Veteran receives his medals 80 years late. Ian Hart was finally honoured at a ceremony in Tamborine Mountain, Queensland, eight decades after his service. Fifth: Personalised vaccine cuts melanoma's return risk by 42%. In a phase 3 trial, a personalised mRNA vaccine given with immunotherapy cut the risk of relapse or death by 42% over two years. Longer follow-up and approval are still needed. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
